beliefs: f shifts the first character forward by one: lowercase a-z and uppercase A-Z wrap around, digits 0-9 wrap around, other characters unchanged [E1, E2, E3, E4]
f leaves the middle characters (positions 1..n-1) unchanged [E1, E2, E3, E4]
f appends a literal 'y' to the end of the string, regardless of the last character [E1, E2, E3, E4]
The trailing 'y' is always appended, not a shifted last character: 'abcy'->'bbcy' and '9'->'9y' confirm this [E2]
There is no special case for input 'y': 'y'->'z' (shifted, no append) and 'yy'->'zy' show 'y' is just shifted like any first char, and the append still happens for length>1 [E4]
When the first character is a digit, it is NOT shifted: '0a'->'0ay', '9z'->'9zy', '0 0'->'0 0y', '123'->'123y' [E1, E3]
The trailing 'y' is appended for all non-empty inputs including digit-first ones ('0a'->'0ay', '9'->'9y') [E1, E2, E3]
